problem: Calculate the second derivative of  $f(s)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡2s,\,{s}^{4}+10s,\,55⟩$ with respect to $s.$

examples.knowledge_point: The Second Derivative of a Vector-Valued Function
examples.problem: Given that $\mathbf r(t) = \langle t^6,\, t^5\rangle,$ Calculate $\mathbf r''(t).$
examples.worked_solution:
To find the second derivative of a vector-valued function, we find the second derivatives of the components.

- For $x(t) = t^6,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) & =6{t}^{5} \\ {x}^{″}(t) & =30{t}^{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

- For $y(t) = t^5,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =5{t}^{4} \\ {y}^{″}(t) & =20{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨{x}^{″}(t),\,{y}^{″}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨30{t}^{4},\,20{t}^{3}⟩ \\  & =10⟨3{t}^{4},\,2{t}^{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
We find ${f}^{′}(t)$ by differentiating each component:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+5{t}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{tan}⁡t) \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({6}^{t})\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{t}^{2}+10t \\ {sec}^{2}⁡t \\ {6}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
